name: Waterflooding and low-salinity water injection
principle: Water is injected to hold pressure and sweep oil; without injection only about 30% of oil is typically recovered. Low-salinity injection swaps divalent cations bound to clay for sodium, freeing oil; BP estimated about 42 million barrels extra at Clair Ridge (640 million barrels recoverable in total).

process_steps.name: Filter and treat injection water (to about 2 micrometres)
Produce oil and recycle produced water

performance.basis: BP estimate versus seawater flooding; 640 million bbl total recoverable

source.note: Offshore Technology, Liquid assets: BP deploys reduced salinity water injection (2012)

costs.basis: dollar year not stated; development cost GBP 4.5 billion

source.note: Offshore Technology, Liquid assets: BP deploys reduced salinity water injection (2012)

advantages: LoSal adds recovery with the same wells
limitations: Scaling and corrosion risk in injection lines
The Offshore Technology article (2012) gives no salinity ppm or percentage-point gain
